body.en: Factoring rewrites a polynomial as a product of simpler factors — the key step in solving equations, finding roots, and simplifying rational expressions.

Always take out the greatest common factor (GCF) first. Difference of squares: \( a^{2}-b^{2}=(a-b)(a+b) \). Monic trinomial: \( x^{2}+(p+q)x+pq=(x+p)(x+q) \). For \( ax^2 + bx + c \), use the \( ac \)-method.

body.en:
Factor completely: \( 3x^3 - 75x \).

First extract the greatest common factor (GCF), \( 3x \):

\[ 3x(x^2 - 25). \]

Recognize \( x^2 - 25 \) as a difference of two squares \( a^2 - b^2 = (a-b)(a+b) \):

\[ 3x(x - 5)(x + 5). \]

Factor by grouping: \( 2x^3 + 6x^2 + 5x + 15 \).

Group into pairs:

\[ (2x^3 + 6x^2) + (5x + 15). \]

Factor out common terms from each group:

\[ 2x^2(x + 3) + 5(x + 3). \]

Factor out the common binomial factor \( (x + 3) \):

\[ (x + 3)(2x^2 + 5). \]

label.en: Common Pitfall — Sum of Squares & Stopping Early

body.en: Two frequent mistakes in factoring: 1. Stopping too early: After factoring out a GCF or one factor, always inspect the remaining polynomial to see if it factors further (e.g. \( x^4 - 16 = (x^2 - 4)(x^2 + 4) = (x - 2)(x + 2)(x^2 + 4) \)). 2. Sum of squares trap: Difference of squares \( a^2 - b^2 \) factors into \( (a - b)(a + b) \), but a sum of squares \( a^2 + b^2 \) is prime over real numbers — it does NOT equal \( (a + b)^2 \)!

label.en: Worked Example D — Algebraic Structure & Vieta's Root Relations

body.en:
Solve the quadratic equation \( x^2 - 10x + 25 = 0 \) and verify the sum and product of its roots.

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Factor into binomials: \( (x - 5)(x - 5) = 0 \implies x = 5 \text{ or } x = 5 \).
  2. Check Vieta's formulas: sum \( = 5 + 5 = \mathbf{10} \) and product \( = (5)(5) = \mathbf{25} \).

solution.en:
Use the \( ac \)-method. We seek two integers whose product is \( a \cdot c = 6(-10) = -60 \) and whose sum is \( b = 11 \).

The factor pair of \( -60 \) that sums to \( 11 \) is \( 15 \) and \( -4 \) (since \( 15 \times (-4) = -60 \) and \( 15 + (-4) = 11 \)).

Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping:

\[ 6x^2 + 15x - 4x - 10 = 3x(2x + 5) - 2(2x + 5). \]

Factor out the binomial \( (2x + 5) \):

\[ (2x + 5)(3x - 2). \]

question.en: Factor the polynomial completely by grouping: \(2x^3 - 3x^2 - 8x + 12\).

solution.en:
Group terms in pairs:

\[(2x^3 - 3x^2) - (8x - 12).\]

Factor out the greatest common factor from each pair:

\[x^2(2x - 3) - 4(2x - 3).\]

Factor out the common binomial \((2x - 3)\):

\[(x^2 - 4)(2x - 3).\]

Recognize \((x^2 - 4)\) as a difference of squares and factor completely:

\[(x - 2)(x + 2)(2x - 3).\]

question.en: [Factoring Polynomials · Practice 3] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 5t + 5 \), evaluate \( g(8) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 50 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 8 \): \( g(8) = 5(8) + 5 = \mathbf{45} \). Setting \( 5t + 5 = 50 \) gives \( 5t = 45 \implies t = \mathbf{9} \).

question.en: [Factoring Polynomials · Practice 4] If the governing relation for this system is \( g(t) = 6t + 6 \), evaluate \( g(10) \) and find the inverse input \( t \) when \( g(t) = 72 \).

solution.en: Substitute \( t = 10 \): \( g(10) = 6(10) + 6 = \mathbf{66} \). Setting \( 6t + 6 = 72 \) gives \( 6t = 66 \implies t = \mathbf{11} \).
